subject: Observability + SIEM integration for Acme on-prem deployment: proposed plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: security@acme-fin.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-20T09:15:00Z
Subject: Observability + SIEM integration for Acme on-prem deployment: kickoff

Hi Ruth / Acme SecOps team,

Following our onboarding call, I wanted to capture a short checklist and ask a few clarifying questions so we can scope the private deployment telemetry handoff. Our goal is to ensure Redwood Private can emit logs/metrics/traces in a way that fits into your existing SIEM and monitoring pipelines without exposing data off your VPC.

High-level asks:
- Do you want agentless forwarding from Redwood to an on-prem collector (TLS to internal endpoint), or do you prefer to pull logs from a file mount?
- Which SIEM product/version are you running (Splunk Enterprise 8.x, Azure Sentinel, Elastic Stack)? Any preferred sourcetypes/ingestion formats?
- Retention & filtering: sample retention policy (events/day) and PII redaction expectations.

What we can offer:
- TLS-forwarded syslog/HTTP intake to your collector with mutual TLS and client cert auth.
- Structured JSON event payloads for audit events, request/response summaries, and tokenized latency metrics.
- Trace hook support (W3C TraceContext) to inject Redwood request IDs and span IDs; we can propagate headers through model inference stack.
- Configurable trimming and PII redaction rules (we'll supply templates).

I attached a short checklist (redwood-siem-integration-checklist.xlsx) and a proposed trace-hook spec for your review. Can we schedule a 30-minute architecture review next week to finalize transport and firewall rules? I propose Tue 2026-06-23 15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood-siem-integration-checklist.xlsx, trace-hook-proposal.md

From: Ruth Patel <ruth.patel@acme-fin.com>

Cc: Dan Lee <dan.lee@acme-fin.com>, security@acme-fin.com
Date: 2026-06-21T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability + SIEM integration for Acme on-prem deployment: kickoff

Vivek — thanks for the overview and the checklist. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) SIEM: We run Splunk Enterprise 8.2 with a heavy reliance on HTTP Event Collector (HEC) for ingest. We have a dedicated index for vendor telemetry (index=vendor_telemetry). Sourcetype conventions are important for our dashboards; we prefer source="redwood_inference" and sourcetype="redwood:events" for structured JSON.

2) Transport: preferred path is mutual-TLS to an internal HEC endpoint (no public egress allowed). If mutual-TLS isn't possible from Redwood runtime in your private bundle, we can accept forwarding to a local collector VM in the VPC.

3) Retention: initial retention for vendor telemetry is 90 days. PII: we cannot accept raw user prompts. We need redaction at source (or tokenized hashes). Please confirm which fields Redwood can redact client-side.

4) Trace correlation: we'd like to map Redwood request_id to our transaction_id. W3C headers are fine; we'll provide our mapping rules.

I'm copying Dan (platform) and our security alias. Tue 06/23 15:00 PT looks OK — hold for final invite. Attached is our telemetry questionnaire (acme-telemetry-questionnaire.pdf) with a few items filled.

Ruth Patel
Head of Security Integrations — Acme Financial Services
ruth.patel@acme-fin.com

---
Attachment: acme-telemetry-questionnaire.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ruth Patel <ruth.patel@acme-fin.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Dan Lee <dan.lee@acme-fin.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability + SIEM integration for Acme on-prem deployment: kickoff

Thanks Ruth — very helpful. Quick technical answers and a proposed transport template below. Please find the checklist and trace-hook spec attached again.

Transport options (ranked preference):
1) HEC (mutual TLS) -> Redwood runtime initiates TLS to your HEC endpoint. We will present a client cert and validate server cert.
   - Port: 8088 (default HEC) or your configured HEC TLS port.
   - IPs: we'll provide CIDR blocks for firewall rules; we can also use customer-assigned egress NAT IPs if you prefer (we support static egress IP on Dedicated/Private).
2) Local collector VM (syslog or file) -> Pull logs from mounted file or accept HTTPS push from Redwood.

Payload shape (JSON recommended):
- timestamp, request_id, span_id, model, route, outcome (success/error), latency_ms, token_count, truncated_prompt_hash, metadata (key:value map)
- We will redact prompt text by default when configured; we can instead send prompt_hash and token_count.

PII redaction: Redwood can redact at ingestion hooks (client-side) for the following fields: prompt_text, user_email, user_ssn_patterns. We will supply regex templates and a verification checklist.

Trace correlation: we will inject traceparent and tracestate per W3C TraceContext. Redwood request_id will be included as attribute "redwood.request_id" in span payloads to map to your transaction_id.

Firewall / auth template (for your ops):
- Allow outbound TCP to HEC host(s) on port 8088 (or configured port) from the Redwood runtime egress IPs: 34.210.12.0/28, 34.210.12.16/28 (example — will provide finalized ranges in PRD).
- TLS: mutual TLS with client cert CN=redwood-client; CA chain managed by Acme.

Action items for Redwood team (assignments):
- @mina_haddad: produce firewall/IP list and static egress options.
- @marissa_cole: finalize trace hook headers and small example service to validate header propagation.

I'll prepare a short architecture review agenda and send a calendar invite for Tue 06/23 15:00 PT.

Cheers,
Vivek

Attachments: redwood-siem-integration-checklist.xlsx, trace-hook-proposal.md

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-24T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability + SIEM integration for Acme on-prem deployment: kickoff

Adding a short rollout template and two small notes from the infra side.

Rollout stages (proposed):
1) Staging validation (2 days): Redwood Private in your staging VPC -> push JSON events to a staging HEC endpoint. Verify sourcetype and index mapping.
2) Canary (1 week): Route 10% of inference traffic to pipeline with telemetry enabled to measure event rates and cost.
3) Full cutover: enable across production clusters after sign-off.

Infra notes:
- Static egress: we can assign a static NAT IP per Dedicated/private deployment; please confirm if Acme teams prefer us to use their NAT or ours.
- Buffering: Redwood uses bounded local buffering (configurable) for temporary network outages — default retention for buffered events is 2 hours. If you need persistent buffers, we'll need to provision an on-VPC collector.

Marissa — quick question on trace headers: can you confirm that the runtime will emit both traceparent and an additional header "x-redwood-request-id" for easy mapping in Splunk? I sketched a tiny example in trace-hook-proposal.md.

Mina Haddad
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

- 7m: Event schema & PII redaction strategy (Marissa)

Pre-meeting asks:

Links for reviewers: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONPREM/ACME+SIEM+Integration, https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ONPREM-3245

Best,
Vivek
